04/How it works

Four steps from idea to shipped.

Three of them every AI builder promises. The fourth only a real repo can keep.

pipilot · acme-bookings4 STEPS
  1. 01read the promptprompt.md
  2. 02wrote screens, wired auth + dbsrc/
  3. 03published a live linkhere.now
  4. 04committed to your Drivedrive://acme-bookings

  1. Describe it.

    Plain words: a web app, a mobile app, a desktop tool, an API. Attach a sketch, a screenshot or a repo.

  2. Watch it build.

    The agent plans, writes and wires a running project, with a live preview you can click while it works.

  3. Ship it.

    Refine in chat, then ship — a live URL, an installer, an APK, or your own host.

  4. Keep it.

    It’s a real repo in your Google Drive. Push it to GitHub, export it, keep building. Nothing is locked in.

It is a real repo. Real files, real git history, real dependencies. On Pilot you push it to your own GitHub and deploy it to your own Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare account, and your PiPilot Cloud (a Postgres backend) can be claimed into your own account and kept. If you leave, you leave with the codebase and the database.

Yes, and it does not expire — no card, unlimited projects, the full builder, live preview, PiPilot Cloud (a Postgres backend) and instant deploy. It is metered rather than crippled: 5 AI prompts a day on a model pool shared with every other free account, and 2 Cloud Hours a month for cloud missions and deploys. That is sized to prove an idea, not to run a product people depend on.

Yes. Real Android and iOS builds through EAS, with Google Play and App Store submission, and Windows, macOS and Linux desktop installers — not a website in a wrapper.

No. Every app gets PiPilot Cloud — a real Postgres backend provisioned in seconds, with tables, SQL, auth and a REST Data API. No signup, no connection string, and the agent creates tables and runs queries as it builds. Claim it into your own account to keep it.

They build web apps and host your code. You can leave with everything.
